items.summary: 量子位·AI与具身智能智库一手报道：韦东奕再获大奖！攻克近140年数学难题，获两位院士共同提名。国内顶尖 AI 智库，深度拆解大模型架构、AI Agent 与具身智能机器人突破。
items.content:
新一届北京市科学技术奖颁出，北京大学数学科学学院长聘副教授、研究员韦东奕荣获杰出青年中关村奖。

该奖项设立于2019年，专门奖励具有引领未来科技发展巨大潜力的青年科学家，每年授奖人数不超过30人。

此次共有29名青年科学家获奖，其中，韦东奕由两位中国科学院院士文兰、王诗宬共同提名，50万元奖金全部归个人所有。

同期获奖的还有专攻肿瘤精准诊疗的朱华研究员、深耕无人集群协同控制的李忠奎教授等，北大共占三席。

在北大新闻网的介绍中，韦东奕最具代表性的科研成果之一，就是与陈琦、章志飞合作攻克了流体力学领域一道悬而未决近140年的经典数学难题——管道Poiseuille流在大雷诺数情形下的线性稳定性。

目前，相关论文和成果已发表于CPAM、Annales ENS、Advances in Mathematics、ARMA等国际著名数学顶刊。

可随着水龙头越拧越大，原本乖乖往下流的水柱就可能开始翻滚、乱窜，水花四溅。

早在1883年，英国物理学家雷诺（Osborne Reynolds）就做过一场经典实验。

他往着一根流着水的透明玻璃管中注入染色液体，并观察它在不同流速下的运动轨迹。

随着流速加快，这根细线开始扭曲、扩散，甚至整个管道里的水都被染上了颜色。

items.summary: 量子位·AI与具身智能智库一手报道：DeepSeek APP突然更新账单，网友：要收费了？。国内顶尖 AI 智库，深度拆解大模型架构、AI Agent 与具身智能机器人突破。
items.content:
眼尖的小伙伴们突然发现，DeepSeek网页和App端的回复下方，悄咪咪地多了一个形似一摞硬币的小图标。

点开一看，好家伙，刚才跟DeepSeek聊的这几句值多少钱，全给你算明白了。

本轮消耗额度、输入（缓存命中/未命中）及输出Token的单价、用量、金额，全都列得清清楚楚。

最下边甚至还配了个上下文占用进度圈，连聊到现在占用了多少上下文空间都能一眼看到。

结合前阵子DeepSeek给免费用户限额冲上热搜的事，不少小伙伴已经开始猜测，大肥鱼是不是已经在为收费做准备了？

有人调侃，梁文锋这波操作，是想让前阵子因为限额而骂他的免费用户们，亲眼看看自己到底消耗了多少算力。（doge）

看到消息后，我第一时间跑去实测了一波，发现大肥鱼网页和App端确实都已经上线了这个功能。

再翻出网页端一轮输入超1.3万Token的对话，账单显示约0.0088元，也才不到一分钱。

顺着账单仔细一扒后我发现，这套计价规则咱们其实并不陌生，与DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash的API空闲时段定价正好对得上。

按照空闲时段的价格，每百万Token输入（缓存命中）仅需0.02元、输入（缓存未命中）需1元，输出则需4元。

items.title: 【量子位AI】刚刚，首个带跨任务空间记忆的原生基模开源！机器人端侧就能跑
items.summary: 量子位·AI与具身智能智库一手报道：刚刚，首个带跨任务空间记忆的原生基模开源！机器人端侧就能跑。国内顶尖 AI 智库，深度拆解大模型架构、AI Agent 与具身智能机器人突破。
items.content:
地下停车场巡检两公里，哪怕每百米只偏半米，一路累积回到起点地图就错位十米；明明是同一根立柱却出现两次，后续定位导航全都乱套。

接到第一个指令，机器人走遍整个办公室，终于找到了角落里的打印机。第二回，要找的打印机明明上一次路过时就见过，机器人却毫无印象，又一次从头找起。

很明显，左边的画面里，一路累积的漂移在模型自纠偏之后，前后拍到的通道对得更齐了。右边的机器人换了任务，依旧能调用之前的三块局部空间记忆。

而且！无一例外，都是把空间记忆直接打包塞进了机器人通用大脑，也就是蚂蚁一直讲的具身原生。

好处也很明显，「一回生二回熟」，机器人干活更高效了，还能像人一样端上铁饭碗，同一个地方能一直干下去。

就连SLAM领域的泰斗级人物、帝国理工学院教授Andrew Davison 都亲自下场点赞——Looks impressive！

但缺点也有，这样跑实在太依赖前期准备了。。。换个地点、目标，原来的通道和点位就得跟着变。

单个RGB摄像头不停送来画面，模型同步估出相机的位置、朝向和画面中物体的深度，再把看到的空间接起来。

今年4月开源的LingBot-Map 1.0已经可以做到，走出去一小段，地图也能跟着往前画。

难就难在怎么把这一段和下一段接起来，还不出错。要是初始位置就估偏了，后面的画面也会沿用这个参照，误差就可能大到从轨迹和点云里看出来。

items.title: 【量子位AI】钛动科技 × 腾讯云达成战略合作，用AI打开企业全球增长新空间
items.summary: 量子位·AI与具身智能智库一手报道：钛动科技 × 腾讯云达成战略合作，用AI打开企业全球增长新空间。国内顶尖 AI 智库，深度拆解大模型架构、AI Agent 与具身智能机器人突破。
items.content:
11月26日，全球领先的AI营销科技公司钛动科技与腾讯云签署战略合作协议。根据协议，双方将围绕专业营销大模型、算力及云基础设施、MaaS服务、腾讯 WorkBuddy 智能体生态等领域深化协同，推动AI与云技术能力同全球品牌出海场景深度融合，为更多企业提供可复制、可规模化的业务增长能力。

钛动科技创始人兼 CEO 李述昊，腾讯集团高级执行副总裁、云与智慧产业事业群（CSIG）CEO 汤道生共同见证，钛动科技AI副总裁陈德品、腾讯云副总裁许华彬分别代表双方签署战略合作协议，钛动科技品牌公关副总裁张羽雪、钛极模型负责人丁俊玮、运维总监肖胜龙，以及腾讯云泛互行业解决方案总经理陈亮、腾讯云互联网出海行业商务总监赵佳楠等双方代表出席了签约仪式。

钛动科技创始人兼CEO李述昊（左二）与腾讯集团高级执行副总裁、云与智慧产业事业群（CSIG）CEO汤道生（右二）；钛动科技AI副总裁陈德品（左一）、腾讯云副总裁许华彬（右一）

钛动科技创始人兼CEO李述昊表示：“企业需要有用的 AI（Useful AI）。这样的AI要能理解业务、主动发现机会，最终交付可衡量的商业结果。依托‘钛极’专业大模型与 Navos Pro 营销多智能体，钛动科技已经在企业出海营销场景中验证了这条路径。此次与腾讯云深化战略合作，我们希望双方携手推动AI促进业务增长形成规模化效应，让更多企业在全球市场实现持续增长。”

腾讯集团高级执行副总裁、云与智慧产业事业群（CSIG）CEO 汤道生表示：“AI的产业价值，需要技术平台与行业伙伴共同创造。钛动科技拥有行业领先的AI营销专业技术积淀、丰富的全球营销场景和实践经验。腾讯云将发挥算力、云基础设施与生态优势，与钛动科技深化协同，推动AI融入企业经营，为全球商业增长创造更多可能。”

腾讯集团高级执行副总裁、云与智慧产业事业群（CSIG）CEO汤道生向钛动科技创始人兼CEO李述昊赠送纪念礼品

作为全球领先的AI营销科技公司，钛动科技以自研钛极专业大模型为底座，打造了以专业智能体Navos Pro为核心的产品矩阵，依托Professional（专业）、Proactive（主动）、Profitable（盈利）三大核心能力，为出海企业提供从市场洞察、内容生成到广告投放与效果优化的端到端服务。当前，钛动科技业务已覆盖200多个国家和地区，累计服务数十万品牌出海，连接约700万家媒体平台及超1.5亿个达人资源，是Google、Meta、TikTok、OpenAI等全球商业平台的核心合作伙伴。

其中，钛极专业大模型在营销推理与多模态理解等领域接连取得亮眼成绩，以全球领先的专业大模型技术竞争力，为双方合作提供了坚实的技术支撑。2026年1月，钛极旗下Tec-Chi-Think在全球知名权威中文大模型综合测评平台SuperCLUE营销专业榜单拿下全球第一；同年7月，钛极旗下 Tec-Chi-VL夺得SuperCLUE出海营销视频理解榜单全球第二。

钛极专业大模型的训练与推理，早已全面运行在腾讯云之上，双方打通了从算力底座、模型训练调优平台、TokenHub 大模型调度，到WorkBuddy生态的Agent—Skill协同的全链路。2026年8月，腾讯 WorkBuddy 技能市场接入钛动科技的“Tec-Do 2.0广告与增长情报”Skill集合，让专业营销智能成为企业日常经营可随时调用的生产力工具。

作为国际顶尖云厂商，腾讯云清晰聚焦 “AI算力底座+行业大模型 / 智能体落地”，重点布局具身智能、自动驾驶、金融、医疗、出海外贸五大高价值方向。其中，出海赛道对合规、本地化、业务闭环的高要求，使其成为腾讯云重点攻坚的方向。此次腾讯与钛动科技达成战略合作，是产业算力底座与AI增长力量在出海赛道的强强联合。

items.summary: 11 月 27 日，蚂蚁灵波科技发布流式三维重建模型 LingBot-Map 2.0
items.content:
11 月 27 日，蚂蚁灵波科技发布流式三维重建模型 LingBot-Map 2.0

11 月 27 日，蚂蚁灵波科技发布流式三维重建模型 LingBot-Map 2.0，并开源带空间记忆的导航模型 LingBot-Navi，进一步补强了蚂蚁灵波具身原生通用大脑的空间记忆与自主导航能力。其中LingBot-Map 2.0 负责从单目 RGB 连续画面中实时重建三维空间，并在模型内部随时修正积累的漂移误差。LingBot-Navi 则依托 LingBot-Map 2.0，构建可跨任务复用的三维空间记忆，按自然语言指令快速查找目标、规划路线，并导航至目标附近的停靠点。

两款模型分别针对机器人长距离建图易漂移、跨任务导航记不住路这两大行业痛点，让机器人能在陌生大场景中边走边建图、随时校准空间记忆、对环境越走越熟悉。

自主移动是机器人进入真实物理世界的基础能力。无论是仓储搬运、园区巡检，还是楼宇配送、家庭服务，都要求机器人在大范围陌生环境中长时间连续作业，并在后续同一场景重复作业时更加高效。例如，机器人进入一间陌生门店，既要边走边认清货架、商品与通道，还要记住路线与周边物品，在接到下一项任务时，可以复用此前看到的环境信息。

但当前主流方案往往卡在两道关口：一方面，长距离流式建图容易不断累积误差，一旦空间记忆错位，后续规划就会跟着出错，通常必须外接优化后端才能纠偏，且外接优化后端只能校正输出轨迹，不会修正模型内部的空间记忆，机器人继续行进时依旧会基于这份已经产生偏差的记忆做出错误判断；另一方面，多数导航模型停留在单次任务视角，每次接到新指令都要从零探索，无法复用已有经验。

针对这一断层，蚂蚁灵波此次发布的两款模型，打通了从“大场景高精建图”到“靠空间记忆导航”的完整链路。

作为今年 4 月开源的 LingBot-Map 1.0 的全新升级版，LingBot-Map 2.0 补上了长距离建图中最关键的一环——纠偏。

此前，LingBot-Map 1.0 凭借仅用单个普通 RGB 摄像头即可边走边实时建图的能力，开源后即登上 GitHub Trending，目前 Star 数已接近 1.9 万，获得全球开发者认可，被广泛应用于机器人巡检、农场建图、三维记录、影视运镜等真实场景。

在此基础上，LingBot-Map 2.0 让模型能够在行进途中随时修正自身空间记忆里的积累误差，这套校正由模型推理原生完成，无需外接地点检索模块或位姿图优化后端：它改写的是模型内部记忆，而不只是修正输出轨迹；每一次校正，既对齐已经走过的路线，也让后续规划建立在更准确的记忆之上。

在 7 个公开数据集、9 项评测设定中，LingBot-Map 2.0 的在线模式几乎在所有指标上均优于现有流式方法，单张 RTX 5090 推理速度达 27.51 帧/秒；触发一次记忆修正后，其表现不仅超越“流式模型+外部回环后端”方案，还在多数基准上领先离线模型。

items.summary: 英伟达面临着改变行事方式的压力，《华尔街日报》的一份新报告显示了它的进展情况。（来源：TechCrunch·前沿AI与硬件）
items.content:
英伟达面临着改变行事方式的压力，《华尔街日报》的一份新报告显示了它的进展情况。

据《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达已告知包括戴尔和超微在内的制造合作伙伴，在评估其区域合作伙伴是否满足美国出口要求的同时，暂停向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和印度尼西亚的服务器发货，具体时间未确定。

至于为什么这些国家的中国公司一直在从这些国家的数据中心远程利用英伟达芯片，据报道，美国商务部本月早些时候勉强堵住了这个漏洞。 《华尔街日报》指出，智库进步研究所估计，此类远程数据中心约占中国人工智能计算能力的 24%。

Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.

According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.

GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ($2 billion).

The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.

Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda, who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.”

Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids.

“We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder, managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.

That’s because GTA VI was created entirely without generative AI.

“We’re kind of at this technological moment where this way of developing has sort of reached its natural frontier,” Feder said. “I don’t think you can say that games like this will always be around.”

As millions of people immersed themselves in Vice City, the tech industry witnessed another long-awaited moment: Anthropic became the first major AI lab to go public. At Nasdaq HQ, Anthropic executives gathered to celebrate the Claude maker’s $81.3 billion IPO. At virtually the same moment that Anthropic broke the record for the largest IPO ever, GTA VI was also breaking records with the highest-rated and best-selling game launch of all time.

But when the Anthropic team rang the bell on Thursday, the sound also signaled the end of an era in video game development, and perhaps even in the arts at large.

Talk to Claude Code without making a sound. Press a button above the prompt, mouth a phrase at your webcam, press again, and the words appear in the prompt box. A lip-reading model (Auto-AVSR) runs locally on your Mac: no audio is recorded and no video leaves your machine.

This is a prototype, and accuracy is modest. Lip reading is hard, and silent mouthing is harder than speech: expect word errors, especially on technical terms, so read the text before you send it. Claude is told which words were lip-read (with the model's other readings), so it reads them in context and asks before acting on anything destructive.

Recognition uses Auto-AVSR's visual-only model vsr_trlrs2lrs3vox2avsp_base: 250M parameters, trained on 3,291 hours of video (LRS2, LRS3, VoxCeleb2, AVSpeech).

¹ Auto-AVSR model zoo: 20.3% word error rate on LRS3 (audio models: 1–2%).

Why it is lower here than on the benchmark:

What helps: short phrases, facing the camera in even light, mouthing a little more clearly than you would speak, and training it on your lips. Training checks how many words it gets wrong on held-out phrases, before and after, and keeps the personal model only when it gets fewer wrong, and ⚙ Settings → 🕘 History shows what the model read and what else it considered, so you can see your own accuracy.

Voice dictation needs you to speak out loud. Typing needs your hands and attention. Silent dictation fits the moments in between:

Install the plugin. In a terminal session of Claude Code:

In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box → Plugins → Add marketplace batanus/lip-dictation → Add plugin.

Press 📹 Set up lip dictation above the prompt (or run /lip-setup). It shows the download size and the model's license terms, and starts only when you press Install. Nothing needs to be installed first: setup fetches what is missing (Python, its packages, the model) into ~/.cache/lip-dictation, about 1.5 GB, with a progress bar above the prompt. If your Mac lacks Apple's Command Line Tools, their installer opens; finish it and press Set up again.

开幕首日，具微科技展台迎来众多专业观众。现场四足机器人依次完成360° 连续旋转、复杂地形跃障与定点跨障跳跃等动态演示，呈现整机运动性能；展台同期展出面向特种具身场景的新一代产品MOVENEW P3S。

与多数以运动演示为主的四足机器人不同，P3S面向工业高危环境设计，定位为可拓展的“工业特种作业移动底座”，而非单一巡检设备，可搭载检测、清障、搬运、处置等任务模块。

P3S整机采用宽体短腿、四轮足构型，铺装路面优先以轮式模式巡航，复杂地形切换足式越障，支持原地转向；负载模式包括100 kg连续行走与爬楼、300 kg重载模式、400 kg低趴模式动态负载、600 kg静态极限负载等四种模式；轮式最高速度5m/s，可通行 ±45° 坡道、35cm连续台阶与150cm单级高台，本体防护等级IP67、轮部IP68，工作温度覆盖 -40℃～85℃，可适配防爆、防磁、防水、防冻等极端工况。

据具微科技相关负责人介绍，P3S从底层FOC驱动到上层规划决策均为全栈自主研发，运动控制器闭环频率达1000Hz以上。MICPCI感控一体架构在端侧直连多源感知与实时控制，承担系统“快反射”；MicVLC工业大脑负责建图、规划与任务路由，完成“慢思考”。快慢两层解耦运行，在保障控制实时性的同时，为后续智能迭代预留空间。

整机动力核心为MICPOW 106扁线关节模组，单机搭载16个。P3S液冷版本将液冷作为架构级设计引入具身本体，是行业内首个落地具身机器人本体的整机液冷方案。公开研究显示，液冷散热效率可达风冷的10～50倍，可将关节核心温度由约100℃降至60℃以下，提升持续输出扭矩与设备使用寿命；在关节扭矩80～120N・m阶梯工况下，扭矩密度提升约100%，缓解长时间连续重载作业中的散热约束。

该产品是面向户外非结构化场景的具身智能模块化载荷补给基站，承担轮足式全域移动智能体的后勤枢纽与边缘算力节点，集成模块化载荷存储、自主换装、自动化能源补给与本地边缘调度能力，形成覆盖“作业执行—后勤补给—任务调度”的无人化作业闭环：机器人自主驶入基站，完成工具更换与能源补给后再次出发。

展会现场，P3S完成全流程无人化实景演示：从起点自主导航出发，识别并绕过障碍抵达工位执行任务，低电量时自行返航、趴伏对接充电，满电后再次出发，全程无人工干预。PANDORA基站同步完成机械臂云台的自动拆装换装，用时控制在90秒内。

机器人作业由此无需因能源补给与任务切换中断，客户亦无需为不同任务单独配置设备。现场来自矿山、石化、电解铝与应急领域的专业观众，重点询问交付周期与部署条件。

二者的协同建立在共用的一套分层技术底座之上：从端侧本体控制、边缘调度到云端管理，机器人与基站在统一架构下完成任务流转与资源调度，而非两套独立系统的拼接。

items.summary: 阿维戴维森在青少年时期失去了左手。从那时起，他就装了一些假肢。但他的最新作品有所不同——它连接到了他前臂上部的神经，让他能够感受到压力。多年来，他第一次可以用左肢处理葡萄、鸡蛋和亲人的手等精致物体。（来源：MIT科技评论·底层科技突破）
items.content:
阿维戴维森在青少年时期失去了左手。从那时起，他就装了一些假肢。但他的最新作品有所不同——它连接到了他前臂上部的神经，让他能够感受到压力。多年来，他第一次可以用左肢处理葡萄、鸡蛋和亲人的手等精致物体。

戴维森正在参加犹他大学进行的一项临床试验，他是第九个将这种实验装置植入手臂的人。但他是第一个把它带回家并独立使用的人。

这只手是仿生卢克手臂的一部分，以《星球大战》中的卢克·天行者的名字命名，他在自己的手臂被光剑砍掉后，安装了一只栩栩如生的假肢。该手臂于 2000 年代开发，于 2014 年进行初步试验，并于同年获得 FDA 批准。戴维森参与的试验并不是那么关注手臂本身，而是关注一种将其连接到人的神经系统的新方法。该连接允许用户控制运动

研究人员希望戴维森的经历能够帮助他们回答一些有关该技术的长期存在的问题，包括它在日常生活中到底有多大用处。他们想知道该设备何时有用以及哪里可能会出现故障。他们还想了解它如何影响戴维森的健康以及他的大脑和神经系统。

items.originalContent:
Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand.

Davidson, who is taking part in a clinical trial run by the University of Utah, is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted in his arm. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently.

The hand is part of the bionic LUKE arm, named after Luke Skywalker of Star Wars, who was fitted with a lifelike prosthetic arm after his own was light-sabered off. The arm was developed in the 2000s, initially trialed in 2014, and approved by the FDA that same year. The trial that Davidson is enrolled in isn’t so focused on the arm itself but on a new way to connect it to a person’s nervous system. The connection allows users to control movements and receive feedback about how much pressure they’re applying.

Researchers hope that Davidson’s experiences will help them answer some long-standing questions about the technology, including how useful it really is in day-to-day life. They want to know when the device is helpful and where it might fail. They also want to learn how it might affect Davidson’s well-being as well as his brain and nervous system.

In 2009, when he was 16, Davidson climbed a telephone pole to get the best shot of a sunset. “I climbed about 35 feet up,” he recalls. But he lost his footing as he tried to descend. He grabbed for a wire, which ended up electrocuting him, before he fell to the ground.

The accident resulted in second- and third-degree burns over 37% of his body, says Davidson, “and I broke my back in approximately 50 separate locations.” He also broke eight ribs, and his spinal cord was severed. He’s pretty sure he broke his left wrist, too. But around 10 days later, his left hand—his dominant hand, and the one he’d grabbed the wire with—had started to develop gangrene. It was amputated.

Davidson was ultimately in a coma for around a month. “Once I woke up, they explained to me: You’re paralyzed, you’re never going to walk again, and also, we took your left hand,” he recalls. “A bit of an inconvenience at 16, to say the least.”

Davidson, now 33 and a trauma therapist, went on to have physical therapy and adjusted to life in his changed body. He’s tried a range of prosthetic hands. The first one, which he received a year and a half after his injury, was a basic hook that allowed him to pick things up. It wasn’t fancy, but it gave him “a psychological feeling of returning to being whole,” he says.

The hands he’s tried since have been more advanced—some have allowed him to control individual fingers with muscle movements, for example. Some have been covered by his medical insurance, which allows for replacements around every five years, he says. Others he’s had to buy himself. He bought his third prosthetic hand, for example, from eBay. “It’s funny to think I bought a secondhand second hand,” he says.

A chance encounter with a scientist at a supermarket introduced Davidson to the research team at the University of Utah, which specialized in researching devices that plug into the body. Since 2013, the team had been running a trial of a system that could connect with the nerves of a residual limb, allowing an amputee to control a bionic one. Davidson turned out to be an ideal candidate, says Jake George, director of the university’s neurorobotics lab.

来自科研、教育、创业与产业一线的嘉宾将齐聚现场。他们有着不同的专业背景和人生经历，有人跨越学科边界，有人从科研走向创业，也有人在技术快速迭代中不断寻找新的方向。

三大信用评级机构之一的标准普尔全球评级正在考虑下调英伟达的评级，理由是对该公司的管理和治理实践感到担忧。

S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices.

Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement.

The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.

Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral.

In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported.

A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO.

It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia.

Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct. As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace.

“People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their company. They’re really embarrassed and angry when senior leadership lets them down.”

The consequences of violating the rules aren’t always tangible, but they’re definitely real. Plass gave one example of a company that banned corporate travel to cut costs — only to have its CEO turn up in a VIP box at the Olympics.

“For over a decade afterwards, ‘the Olympics’ was used within that company as an example of the worst thing an employee could do. People would say, ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that, but it’s not like I went to the Olympics.’”

Plass says companies that remove an executive typically do so after an investigation, then try to win back employees. “In most organizations they make a change at the top based on what’s happened,” he said, “and then they will have a hearts-and-minds initiative, to go out to their employee base and their customers and their investors and everybody else, and say, we get it. We’re sorry. We’ve changed. That’s essentially what they do.”

Of course, that playbook is harder to follow at a company like Nvidia, where Huang left without a clear succession plan, and there are serious doubts about whether the company could continue to thrive without him. In cases like that, Plass acknowledges there’s no easy answer.

“I would draw a distinction there between the kind of companies where the CEO is a kind of godhead figure … where the person and the company are almost impossible to separate,” he said. “There it’s much, much harder to deal with.”

In that context, Huang’s stutter-step over the code of conduct is easier to understand. Judging by the employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang’s return hasn’t created a morale problem so far. But as the coming months put more pressure on Huang and his colleagues, sidestepping the code could end up costing Nvidia something harder to measure — its employees’ pride in the company.

Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 反驳了 Anthropic 认为我们应该“让人类自由意志”屈服于人工智能系统的说法。在周三的一篇长篇 X 帖子中，阿莫迪称这个建议“荒谬”。

“我们永远不应该为了效率或安全而牺牲合法性或自决权，”他写道。这种反对专制的论点逐字逐句地反对人工智能的治理，我同样强烈地感到，将治理交给人工智能是一个坏主意……没有人仔细阅读过我的文章或我的采访，可以合理地得出我相信任何不同的东西的结论。

在发表这一声明之前，Anthropic 的竞争对手越来越多地异口同声地表示，如果人工智能的开发不负责任，人类的能动性可能会面临风险。本月早些时候，OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 表示，他希望确保人们继续拥有“未来的代理权”。

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.”

“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.”

The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.”

Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.”

But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power.

Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software.

Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.”

Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research.

In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.”

items.content:
今年圣诞节，圣诞老人不会向纽约孩子们运送任何人工智能聊天机器人玩具。

州长凯西·霍赫尔 (Kathy Hochul) 本周签署了一项法案，禁止未来五年在纽约制造、分销和销售此类玩具。该法案明确针对带有嵌入式或集成人工智能聊天机器人的玩具，例如会说话的毛绒动物、玩偶和依靠互联网让孩子们不停叫闹的机器人。

该法案使纽约州成为继加州之后第二个禁止人工智能玩具的州。

从技术上讲，新法律在签署后 90 天生效，因此一些家长可以尝试在假期前及时满足孩子对像跳跃的菲比这样的令人毛骨悚然的玩具的愿望，但州长敦促他们不要这样做，因为存在风险。根据 Common Se 本周发布的一项新研究，显然，大约四分之一有八岁以下孩子的美国父母要么拥有人工智能玩具，要么正在考虑在这个假期给他们的孩子一个人工智能玩具。

Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas.

Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.

The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.

Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media.

“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”

When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”

When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.

The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem, Lovi, Meemo Bear, BubblePal Panda, and Tavlshero‘s AI Puppy.

The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules.

While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study.

2025 年 5 月，我的同事 David Rotman 撰写了一篇专题报道，描述人工智能如何让我们继续依赖天然气。仅仅 18 个月后，我已经记不清有多少次他的观点被证明是正确的。

当然，从技术上讲，可以通过其他能源来满足世界不断增长的电力需求，包括由电池支持的风能和太阳能等可再生能源。但迄今为止，美国的现实是，数据中心的繁荣正在推动天然气的大规模复苏。

仅举一个例子：大卫在他的故事中重点关注的路易斯安那州元数据中心的计划已经扩大，其电力需求也随之扩大。当地公用事业公司从计划的 3 个天然气发电厂增加到 10 个。正如我在本周的一篇新报道中所写，数据中心开发商现在将目光投向电网之外，并计划建造自己的离网天然气发电厂。我们是怎么到这里的？

如果您想了解电网的未来，一种方法是查看互连队列，即已请求连接到系统的发电厂列表。近年来，这些队列主要由风能和太阳能等可再生能源主导，这通常是当今建设新能源产能最便宜的方式。

In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.

Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.

Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?

If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.

But there’s been a shift in some places, particularly for PJM, the country’s largest power grid operator, which covers parts of 13 states in an area stretching from Illinois to Washington, DC. PJM has seen a major uptick in natural-gas proposals. In August, the operator announced that it had accepted proposals for 715 total projects with a capacity of over 200 gigawatts to join its queue. Nearly half that total capacity represented natural-gas plants.

If all the projects in the queue were built, it would increase the fossil-fuel share on PJM’s grid from 61% to 67%, according to an analysis by Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue.

PJM’s queue is reflective of a bigger trend across the US. Natural gas is already the single biggest source of electricity in the country, and it has basically become the default to meet exploding power demand.

This AI-driven rush is already affecting greenhouse-gas emissions for tech companies. Meta’s emissions are up 45% over last year’s, according to the company’s recently released 2026 Sustainability Report. That’s even higher than the jumps from fellow hyperscalers Google (18%), Amazon (16%), and Microsoft (25%). The company is also “reevaluating” its 2030 goal to reach net-zero emissions, according to the report, though there aren’t details about how or when it might reach a decision there.

And there’s another tidbit in that Meta report worth noting: The company said that when the grid can’t deliver power “on the necessary timeline,” it will look to other methods, including building its own on-site power generation.

This fits into a related and growing trend that I’ve been tracking recently: Data center developers are looking to bypass long wait times to hook up to the grid by building their own power plants instead.
